target_columns.name: product_line
target_columns.transformation: Direct passthrough from joined policies row, grouped

target_columns.name: claim_month
target_columns.transformation: Truncated to first of month via DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(claim_date), MONTH(claim_date), 1)

target_columns.name: status_group
target_columns.transformation: CASE regroup: Approved/Paid -> Settled, Rejected -> Declined, else -> Pending

target_columns.name: claim_count
target_columns.transformation: COUNT(*) of claims rows per group after join and GROUP BY

target_columns.name: total_claim_amount
target_columns.transformation: SUM(claim_amount) per group, rounded to 2 decimal places

quirks: INNER JOIN on policy_id silently drops claims with no matching policy (orphan claims excluded, not flagged as nulls)

Status regrouping CASE is duplicated in SELECT and GROUP BY -- any status not explicitly listed (including NULL) falls into 'Pending' via ELSE, so new/unexpected status values are silently reclassified rather than erroring
DATEFROMPARTS month truncation always sets day=1 -- must use a day-agnostic month-start derivation (e.g. trunc('month')) in the rewrite, not just reformatting

ROUND(SUM(...), 2) applies float rounding after aggregation -- precision/representation differences (float vs decimal) between SAS/SQL and Spark can cause small reconciliation diffs that must be explicitly tolerated/documented, not treated as true mismatches
ORDER BY is cosmetic (claim_month, product_line) and has no effect on aggregated values -- do not treat row order as a reconciliation signal
